items.statement: CAPEX of Rs. 725 crores over next two years, fully funded.
items.quote: Yes, so this CAPEX is to happen over the next two years' time. We have already spent around Rs. 90 crores to 100 crores on this CAPEX in the form of advance, etc. And the rest of the expenditure is to take place over next two years' time. So we are having the entire fund tie-up for this project.

items.statement: Additional depreciation from expansion Rs. 35-40 crores.
items.quote: So, from the expansion side, our additional depreciation would be in the tune of Rs. 35 crores to Rs. 40 crores.

items.statement: Legacy business demand expected to normalize in next two to three quarters.
items.quote: In our legacy business also we are expecting that the demand should return back to normal levels in the next two to three quarters.

items.statement: rPSF volumes expected to remain at Q4 levels in Q1, no further decline.
items.quote: Okay, rPSF numbers, yes, so we are expected to maintain the rPSF numbers in Q1 also as per Q4.

items.statement: rPET volumes in FY26 similar to FY25, significant jump in FY27.
items.quote: So for FY '26, the number could be around that only because our capacity is 42,000 tonnes. And the capacity ramp up will happen by December '25. So it will take two to three months or four months' time in stabilizing. So we do not expect there would be any increase in numbers in this current financial year. But of course there would be a significant jump in FY '27.

items.statement: Scrap bottle prices peaked in April and have started to soften.
items.quote: Yes. So the peak has been achieved in April itself, now the bottle prices have started to soften up.

items.statement: Gap between virgin and recycled granule pricing currently about 30%.
items.quote: The main intense is because of the rising gap between the virgin and the recycled granule pricing, which is presently about 30%.

items.statement: US tariffs creating uncertainties, some positive traction, some feeling heat.
items.quote: Currently, the stand of USA on tariffs is also creating uncertainties on the business, while some are getting positive traction and some are feeling the heat.

items.statement: Legacy business facing heat from higher input prices and suppressed demand.
items.quote: Our legacy business is facing some heat due to the higher input prices as well as suppressed demand from the user industry.

items.statement: Warangal existing capacity optimal utilization expected by Q3-Q4 FY26.
items.quote: Yes, so for existing capacity of Warangal, we are expecting to be optimal utilization by Q3, Q4 of this year. And for the expansion project, our full impact will come from FY '28.

items.statement: FY26 revenue expected Rs. 850-880 crore.
items.quote: Revenue expected to be in the range of Rs. 850 crore to Rs. 880 crore driven by increased volume across both oil and non-oil portfolios and higher ethanol capacity utilization.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA expected Rs. 80-85 crore.
items.quote: EBITDA expected to be in the range of Rs. 80 crore to Rs. 85 crore, supported by improved product mix, operational efficiencies, and higher margin contributions.

items.statement: FY26 PAT expected Rs. 42-48 crore.
items.quote: And PAT expected to be in the range of Rs. 42 crores to Rs. 48 crores, aided by cost rationalization, margin expansion, and improved working capital management.

items.statement: Second phase of ethanol facility to commence by Q3 FY26, adding 180 KL per day.
items.quote: We are now progressing rapidly with the second phase of our ethanol facility, which is on track to commence by Q3 FY ‘26. This expansion will add 180 KL per day to our current capacity, bringing our total ethanol production capacity to 310 KL per day.

items.statement: Received order of Rs. 300 crore for 41,000 KL from OMCs through October 2025.
items.quote: We received an order of Rs. 300 crore for 41,000 KL from various OMCs through to October '25.

items.statement: Ethanol division sustainable EBITDA margin 12-15%.
items.quote: And I have always maintained that given where we are and the way we are operating our Ethanol division, we can maintain between 12% and 15%, and there is a quarterly seasonality on the raw material prices as it is agri-based.

items.statement: Branded division EBITDA margin expected 8.5-9% in FY26.
items.quote: And I think in that same range, we intend to continue this financial year at between 8.5% and 9%.

items.statement: Total ethanol CAPEX will go up to about Rs. 250 crores.
items.quote: Sure, so our total CAPEX will go up to about Rs. 250 crores and yes, we expect about a 3.4 asset turn after expansion once we start the operation.

items.statement: Secured Rs. 88 crore long-term debt from HDFC Bank for second phase expansion.
items.quote: And in the second phase, again, the equity part is being funded through internal accruals, and we have secured an Rs. 88 crore long-term debt, which has already been disbursed.

items.statement: Expects higher revenue in Consumer and Bulk divisions year-on-year.
items.quote: But we are expecting higher revenue, like I said, in the Consumer division and year-on-year also in the Bulk division. So, from that point of view, year-on-year basis, you will see a good quarter.

items.statement: Scaling up Pasta portfolio under Oleev Kitchen brand with celebrity endorsement and targeted advertising.
items.quote: Further, we are scaling up the Pasta portfolio under the Oleev Kitchen brand with celebrity endorsement and targeted advertising. Overall demand is improving, driven by expanded distribution, innovation and new product launches in our food basket.

items.statement: Raw material prices softened by 10% with paddy crop and another 8-10% with FCI rice policy.
items.quote: First, the prices came down by roughly, let's say, 10% when the paddy crop came. And then when the FCI rice policy came, that I mentioned in my opening remarks, prices softened by another 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Expects asset turn of about 3.4x after ethanol expansion.
items.quote: Yes, I mean, you can do the calculations. So, we are expecting an asset turn of about 3.4x after expansion from the full total CAPEX of the Ethanol division, plus the growth from the other two divisions.

items.statement: Above-the-line advertising spend increased to almost 7% in FY25, intends to maintain or increase in FY26.
items.quote: So, above the line we had spent I think close to about 4% which has gone up to almost 7% in FY ‘25 and we intend to maintain that or increase that further in FY ‘26.

items.statement: Ethanol plant running at full capacity utilization currently.
items.quote: As far as the capacity utilization goes, we are running at full capacity utilization currently. And with the expansion coming in, we are expecting higher capacities later in the year.

items.statement: New ethanol capacity expected 50-60% utilization in Q3, gradually increasing to around 90% in Q4.
items.quote: It’s safe to assume around 50–60% utilization in Q3, gradually increasing to around 90% in Q4. It's just an off the cuff calculation, but we will see how it pans out.

items.statement: Expects FY26 to be better than FY25 due to long-term contracts and new vessel.
items.quote: Definitely, the vessels are on long -term contracts. We are adding 1 more vessel to fleet, which is Nusantara. So definitely, FY '26 should be better than FY '25.

items.statement: UK business expected to be cash flow positive from FY27 onwards.
items.quote: In another 12 months to 15 months, the development part in the U.K will be completed. And our expectation is that we will be cash flow positive starting FY '26-'27 onwards.

items.statement: Acquiring MSV NPP Nusantara for $23 million, financed by debt and internal resources.
items.quote: This vessel was built in 2010 and it is being acquired at a cost of $23 million. And this financing will be a mix of debt and our internal resources that we already have in our hand.

items.statement: Swordfish chartered for 730 days at $78,000 per day, effective 21st May.
items.quote: I'm pleased to also announce that the charter for Seamec Swordfish is 730 days and the effective rate is almost $78,000 per day and this remains unchanged during the entire period.

items.statement: All vessels deployed; Barge off-hire from 15th May to 15th October due to monsoon.
items.quote: So as Rajeev ji has earlier told in this address all our vessels are deployed and only one vessel that is Seamec Barge that has completed its long-term contract of 2 years on 15th of May. So during off season, it will remain off hire from 15th May to 15th October being monsoon season.

items.statement: No vessels available for new contracts for next 2-3 years due to existing charters.
items.quote: So as such, I don't have availability of vessels for next 2 to 3 years. And if we can get hold of another expansion by purchase of new vessels, so definitely there is a lot of work in the Gulf coming from Aramco and also coming from ADNOC

items.statement: Incorporated JV Searete India IFSC for vessel leasing, buying, and sale.
items.quote: Further development is that in our wholly owned subsidiary in Dubai, which is Seamec International FZE, we have incorporated a joint venture company in the name of Searete India IFSC Private Limited in the Gift City of India in Ahmedabad, Gujarat and other joint venture partners is a company called Arete Shipping DMCC, which is also a UAE-based company.

items.statement: Seamec Anant vessel from parent HAL Offshore not yet arrived, process ongoing.
items.quote: No, there was only one vessel in the parent company, that is Seamec Anant and as part of the overall structuring that vessel has not yet arrived in Seamec. It is still under process.

items.statement: JV acquiring another cargo vessel for time charter; JV partner 50% equity.
items.quote: And this joint venture, again, is we are acquiring another cargo vessel. And again, we will be putting it on time charter. And the JV partner is the person who has identified the vessel who has brought in the contract, and who will also be a 50% equity partner in this

items.statement: No immediate plans to acquire more assets beyond Nusantara.
items.quote: So right now, the asset that we acquired is getting chartered with ONGC. The other one has now gone to Middle East. So immediately, there are no further plans to acquire more assets.

items.statement: Plans to replace older vessels over next 3-5 years with new vessels.
items.quote: And our plans definitely are to replace these vessels over the next 3 years 5 years with better new vessels as we have purchased Paladin, we have purchased Swordfish.

items.statement: Seamec III working with Hardy Oil on spot basis, extensions possible.
items.quote: Seamec 3 started this particular contract with Asian Energy way back in February 2025. Initial term was 30 days. And after that, there have been extension of 15 days, almost like 4 -5 times.

items.statement: L&T contract $101 million in consortium, Seamec share $30-31 million, completed.
items.quote: So you have rightly mentioned, we have won a contract of $101 million, but this was in consortium with Porsche, Subsea, Singapore. And our share out of this contract was somewhere around US$30 million US$31 million.

items.statement: Swordfish contract with Mermaid reduced rate due to technical snag; only worked days recognized.
items.quote: So they reduced our charter rate from the earlier decided rate because this was not able to do the saturation diving so they shifted it into air diving and they reduced our rate. So whatever work we have performed, whatever number of days we have performed, we have built for only those days.

items.statement: Long-term diving support vessels operate 350 days per year; spot vessels 7 months.
items.quote: So, see all long-term contracts, which are on diving support services run throughout the year. If there is no breakdown, then you can assume full year working for 350 days, that is what we consider, okay?

items.statement: Targets minimum 50% EBITDA growth excluding ESOP cost for next year.
items.quote: A minimum growth of EBITDA of 50% excluding ESOP cost. That's the very, very first target.

items.statement: Aims for at least 300 bps EBITDA percentage improvement next year.
items.quote: We want to increase the quality of our revenues. With that, at least 300 basis points of EBITDA percentage improvement.

items.statement: Aerospace revenue target for FY26 is at least 35% growth.
items.quote: Starting by aerospace, I will say that our target for Fiscal Year '26 is at least 35% growth in revenues.

items.statement: Defense expects growth rate of about 75% moving forward.
items.quote: And right now we are on a very strong growth path. And we expect the growth to be at a rate of about 75% moving forward and also a similar focus on the bottom line also.

items.statement: Defense order book reaching about Rs. 1,800 crores.
items.quote: And our order books are now reaching about Rs. 1,800 crores.

items.statement: ESAI order book close to Rs. 600 crores plus.
items.quote: We are close to Rs. 600 crores plus of order books with us.

items.statement: ESAI is doing a growth of more than 60%.
items.quote: We are doing a growth of 60%, more than 60%.

items.statement: Aims to improve EBITDA margins by about 300 bps each year.
items.quote: We intend to improve our EBITDA margins by about 300 bps each year.

items.statement: Aims to achieve average 24% EBITDA in next 2 to 3 years.
items.quote: With effecti ve execution of product-led strategy, by FY ‘28, the Company aims to invert its current revenue mix of 80% service revenue and 20% product revenue, which will be the key driver for non -linear margin- led growth, with the aim and objective of achieving an average of 24% EBITDA in the next 2 to 3 years

items.statement: Phase-1 facility will cost Rs. 250 crores; Phase-1A Rs. 120 crores.
items.quote: This facility of Phase-1 would cost Rs. 250 crores. And the first Phase-1A of it would cost Rs. 120 crores, which would be mostly through internal funding.

items.statement: Phase-1A CAPEX including building and equipment Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 120 crores, mostly internal accruals.
items.quote: See, as Dr. SRN explained, what we have on the radar, and which is under development where the plan is at an approval stage is Phase-1A where the CAPEX including the building as well as the equipment is going to be anywhere between Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 120 crores. Of which most of it, our objective is that most of it should be through internal accruals.

items.statement: Defense production revenue expected to double in FY26 from Rs. 196 crores.
items.quote: This year FY ‘25 was around Rs. 196 crores. We are talking about probably doubling it in FY ‘26.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin at least 17% average.
items.quote: But I am saying profit after adjusting to EBITDA because we have a huge cost on ESOPs, after adjusting our EBITDA still can be around 50% growth from the current level, and PAT will be proportional and EBITDA margin will be at least at 17% average.

items.statement: FY26 ESOP cost expected around Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores.
items.quote: Around Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected at 26% at Company level.
items.quote: So, 26% is effective tax rate we can expect at the Company level.

items.statement: If economy grows 6-6.5% and no major incident, will try to sustain this kind of growth rate.
items.quote: All I can say at this point in time is, if the economy continues to grow at 6-6.5% and if there's no major sort of incident or episode, then we will try and sustain this kind of growth rate at least.

items.statement: In 99Acres, will continue to invest aggressively in marketing.
items.quote: So in 99Acres, we will continue to invest aggressively in marketing. And I think we've gained significant share in the last six months.

items.statement: Marketing spend in Naukri will continue for some time.
items.quote: But it's helping us meet a strategic long term objectives and it will continue for some time.

items.statement: Jeevansathi will try to break even this year.
items.quote: In Jeevansathi we'll try to break even this year as well. But at the same time, we would want to continue to grow at 20-25%.

items.statement: Jeevansathi aims to grow 20-25% while industry grows 8-10%.
items.quote: The industry will be growing at 8-10%, but we would want to continue to gain share, even in Jeevansathi.

items.statement: JobHai monetization: Rs. 1 crore in March, Rs. 6 crores for the year.
items.quote: We started monetizing last year, small sums, but we did about a crore in March. For the year we did Rs. 6 crores.

items.statement: AI central team headcount grew 5-6X over last four or five years.
items.quote: Now that central team itself is very large, and has grown maybe 5 or 6X in terms of headcount over the last four or five years.

items.statement: AI applied in Jeevansathi and Naukri gave 15-20% kicker in metrics.
items.quote: in Jeevansathi and in Naukri, wherever we've applied the latest sort of models, we've seen a 15-20% kicker in terms of all the metrics we track.

items.statement: Agentic AI offering beta tested in 10-12 companies, moving to commercial testing.
items.quote: And this is being beta tested in about 10 or 12 companies. Now we are moving to the commercial testing phase.

items.statement: Shareholders approved another fund of about Rs. 1,000 crore.
items.quote: As you would have seen that recently, we got the shareholders’ approval for another fund for about Rs. 1,000 crore rupees.

items.statement: Post-carry, post-expense IRR for 2019-20 vintage fund: above 18-19% decent, above 25% excellent.
items.quote: See, the post-carry, post-expense IRR for the 2019-20 vintage fund, anything above 18-19% would be decent, above 25% would be excellent.

items.statement: Dividend might continue to increase as we go ahead.
items.quote: Keeping that in view, I think we have increased the dividend as of now, we might continue even more as we go ahead.

items.statement: In many cases still getting 30-40% jump on what billed client last year.
items.quote: We still continue, in many cases, still getting a 30-40% jump on what we billed the client last year.

items.statement: AI central team may be around 100 people.
items.quote: So the central team, which is the specialized team, that may be let's say 100 people, plus minus.

items.statement: At least 60-70% of what we do has some element of AI.
items.quote: So overall, I would suspect that today, at least 60-70% of what we do has some element of AI in it, in terms of innovation and product development.

items.statement: Aims at least 30-35% sales growth in FY26, moving towards 5-digit sales.
items.quote: So what our plan is, what I have guided is at least 30% to 35% what we have done in FY ’25 and move towards the five-digit number in FY’26.

items.statement: Plans to launch at least half of 18.56 msf pipeline in FY26, possibly double-digit msf.
items.quote: In this financial year alone, which is FY 26, if everything works well, we will be able to launch at least half of this pipeline. In a more optimistic scenario, we can cross the double digit in terms of million square feet launches.

items.statement: Expects to complete 5.5 million square feet in FY26, at least 20% increase.
items.quote: We expect to also increase this by at least 20% next year with 5.5 million square feet in FY ’26.

items.statement: Contracts, manufacturing, and retail revenue expected to grow at least 10% with enhanced profitability next year.
items.quote: On the contracts, manufacturing, and retail side, we concluded the year with a revenue of about Rs. 661 crores. And we expect to grow at least 10% with enhanced profitability next year.

items.statement: Unrecognized revenue has embedded project-level EBITDA margin of 33%, to be recognized over 3-4 years.
items.quote: Our current balance revenue to recognize from already sold unit as on 31st March is Rs. 15,873 crore which is Sobha share, and we expect project level EBITDA margin of 33%.

items.statement: Margins expected to improve significantly in coming year.
items.quote: In coming year, margins are expected to improve significantly.

items.statement: New sales EBITDA margin expected closer to 40%.
items.quote: Current sales, again EBITDA margin should be now in the new one should be closer to 40% is what our sense is, and if it’s our own land in some of the places that also will add to those margins, but if it’ s in a typical joint development and recent acquisitions, we should be in the range between, again closer towards 40%.

items.statement: New land purchases in FY26 similar or slightly higher than FY25, funded by operational cash flow.
items.quote: Well, we should do similar or it’s not a very clear number because what we are going to do in terms of any new deals that can come up, those calls we will take little later but from a current visibility point of view , there would be certain committed land payouts and those will be similar or slightly higher than what we had, but largely from the operational cash flow that we will generate, we sho

items.statement: Good visibility of order book to achieve 10% growth in contracts, manufacturing, and retail.
items.quote: We have good visibility of order book to achieve this and hope to build the order book during the year as well.

items.statement: Like-to-like price increases may not occur; steady pricing with inflation-led increases in Bangalore.
items.quote: Second in the same market from a pricing point of view, like- to-like pricing probably we might not increase the price as we had done in the last couple of years. S o hence we can see a steady pricing environment

items.statement: Residential demand environment steady despite global uncertainties.
items.quote: The residential demand environment seems to be steady at the moment, despite witnessing certain global political and economic uncertainties that have hit us in the past few months in this year.

items.statement: Bangalore demand steady; NCR steady; Kerala good interest from NRIs.
items.quote: Bangalore is largely end-user driven and there the demand seems to be at least steady from the leading indicators which is from enquiries and from the site visits point of view.

items.statement: Core business remains 3-bedroom, 2, 3, and 4 bedroom apartments; large projects have good mix.
items.quote: Yes. I mean like I mentioned earlier as well, it is not that we have deliberately aimed for a certain ticket sizes, those launches that we have done last year where all of them came up in a certain timeframe which was coincidental, but otherwise our core bread and butter business has always been a 3 -bedroom, 2, 3 and 4 bedroom apartments and that continues to be the case even in the future and pa

items.statement: Short-term investor-led bookings may lead to cash flow issues in slowdown; company avoids such demand.
items.quote: One of the things that we have seen is any short -term investor led bookings would might, there is a possibility that it might lead to cash flow issues in case of any steadiness or slowdown in the market, that we would definitely like to avoid and hence due to that nature and second is our pricing being slightly premium, both these take out a large chunk of the market which is pure investor market

items.statement: Completed Rs. 2,000 crore rights issue, received Rs. 1,996 crore, balance Rs. 4 crore outstanding.
items.quote: In FY ’25, we have completed Rs. 2,000 crore size right issue successfully and received Rs. 1996 crore and balance Rs. 4 crore was outstanding as on 31st March.

items.statement: FY26 revenue and profitability expected to be better than FY25.
items.quote: I think it would be better than '24-'25. I cannot quantify today, but it will be better than '24-'25 in terms of the revenue as well as the profitability.

items.statement: Palghar expansion commissioning delayed to Q4 FY27 due to land acquisition.
items.quote: This would be Q4 FY '27 and Q4 FY '28. Q4 '27 would be Palghar and Q4 FY '28 would be Odisha.

items.statement: Value-added products targeted to reach 20% of sales next year.
items.quote: See the next year, we are looking around 20% the value-added product.

items.statement: Value-added products earn 10-15% higher margins than conventional products.
items.quote: See, generally, it is 10% to 15% extra than the normal one.

items.statement: Demand subdued in May due to cyclone and early monsoon; recovery hoped in coming weeks.
items.quote: However, from May onwards, demand was impacted due to heavy rains across several states starting May 20th caused by cyclonic activity in the Arabian Sea and the onset of early monsoon at Kerala from May 23rd. However, we remain optimistic about recovery in the coming weeks.

items.statement: No material price increase taken in Q4 or Q1 due to subdued demand.
items.quote: Q4, it's minimal. I would say this time, hardly any price increase, I would say. The reason is, there may be Rs 1 or Rs 2 increases that may be, in the percentage terms, not more than 1% because the reason is the demand itself is very subdued.

items.statement: No cost increase on fiber; cement prices to normalize in June.
items.quote: As I said, there's no any cost increase on the fiber side. So there is in between price increase happens in the cement. You know that's, again, a different type of industry. But, in June, it will be back.

items.statement: Southern plant utilization expected to increase by 10%.
items.quote: I think there will be 10%-10% extra in both.

items.statement: Gross profit margin unlikely to return to FY21 levels; gradual improvement expected.
items.quote: Unlikely. The reason is that raw material prices for that increase, it is descending at the same price. There's no any reduction. So there's no increase happening now. That is one. And second is unless until the substantially the price increase happens, I don't see we will reach to that level.

items.statement: Normal annual capex at plants is INR15 crores.
items.quote: 15 crores is the normal capex is always in the plants.

items.statement: No new debt for expansions this year; debt already sanctioned for Palghar.
items.quote: We are not raising this year any debt on those expansions because already I spent good amount, and land acquisition is going on. So somewhere in '26 only we will see how my cash flow is. And based on that, we'll raise the debt. But overall, the debt is already sanctioned for the Palghar plant.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation beyond INR85-90 could impact costs; natural hedge from exports.
items.quote: We are not getting impacted if it is within that INR85. It goes above INR85, and that's again, INR90, then definitely would be impacted.

items.statement: Expects double-digit topline growth, beating industry, with bottomline growing better than top.
items.quote: IIL shall always beat the market. We shall continue with our double-digit growth strategy with the topline growth coming majorly from Maharatnas which will mean that the bottomline will increase better than the top.

items.statement: Plans Rs. 100 crores capex in FY26, majorly for Sotanala plant.
items.quote: Here I would also like to talk about our expansion budgets, which for this year we have kept at around Rs. 100 crores FY'26. A major investment is going to go to Sotanala, which is going to be a fully automatic plant.

items.statement: Dahej plant to contribute about Rs. 100 crores this year with over 50% CAGR in 3-4 years.
items.quote: So we come into production and this year this plant is going to contribute roughly about Rs. 100 crores this expansion with a CAGR of more than 50% in next 3 to 4 years because the expectation is very big and our hope from this new expansion is quite big and we'll be launching many new products and increasing our capacity for many products from this new expansion.

items.statement: Plans to launch 6 products in FY26, including patented and collaboration products.
items.quote: We are going to launch 6 products in FY'26 and all these are expected to launch soon. So the first product is going to be Altair, which is a Japanese collaboration 9(3).

items.statement: Expects 200-300 bps EBITDA margin improvement over 2-3 years.
items.quote: But yes, in 2-3 years, definitely we will see 200 to 300 points change actually in the EBITDA levels. So that is going to be --

items.statement: Kaeros expected to generate Rs. 10-12 crores profit this fiscal and Rs. 100 crores revenue.
items.quote: So in this fiscal, we can expect a profit of around Rs. 10 crores-Rs. 12 cores from this Kaeros business, but next year it will multiply.

items.statement: New paddy herbicide Altair expected to achieve Rs. 10-15 crores sales initially, scaling to Rs. 40-50 crores next year.
items.quote: So in terms of value you can anticipate to begin with a modest number of Rs. 10 crores-Rs. 15 crores, but in the second year itself, you can touch Rs. 40 crores-Rs. 50 crores with this product.

items.statement: Expects good demand for herbicides in June due to shortages.
items.quote: So, I can say that June should see a good demand for these herbicides better than usual. So now it depends how much we are able to place.

items.statement: Some price improvement in April-May, with potential further revisions based on season.
items.quote: There has been some price improvement in the month of April, which has gone up to May and there will be another price drop. So that's a regular practice actually.

items.statement: Manpower shortage due to war may impact production and performance.
items.quote: Yes, there is some shortage of manpower. There is some shortage of manpower because when the war started, so people from Jammu fled actually and not only there, there was impact at other plants also because people were worried and they were receiving calls from the peop le in the village, come back to the village

items.statement: Working capital increase due to temporary inventory buildup, expected to improve.
items.quote: Yes, it's temporary because of the inventory buildup and you will see the improvement in the fiscal because we are very very fierce on this.

items.statement: Salary budgets expected to grow at 15% CAGR.
items.quote: But yes, I think we should be able to maintain with 15% CAGR on our salary budgets.

items.statement: Launch pipeline of over 13.5 million square feet planned for FY26.
items.quote: Puravankara is well-positioned to capitalize on these trends with a robust launch pipeline of over 13.5 million square feet, planned for Financial Year ‘25-'26, aiming at centering our presence amid a consolidating market.

items.statement: Expects to receive occupancy certificates for key projects in FY26.
items.quote: Further, we are expecting to receive occupancy certificates during this year, which is '25 -'26 for key projects, such as Capella, Atmosphere, Oakshire, A dora De Goa for which we have already secured OCs for a few phases in the last quarter.

items.statement: Aims to gradually reduce debt per square feet for under-construction projects.
items.quote: Our aim is to gradually reduce debt per square feet especially for projects under construction.

items.statement: Exploring funding options like QIP or platform partnerships to balance capital structure.
items.quote: We also are exploring funding options as we have been communicating with you, like QIP or platform level partnerships to keep our capital s tructure balanced and support our growth plans.

items.statement: Invested Rs. 1,284 crores in land, adding 8 million sq ft and Rs. 13,000 crores GDV.
items.quote: We made significant progress during this financial year with land investment of approximately Rs. 1,284 crores, which added almost 8 million square feet of our development portfolio, representing a GDV value of Rs. 13,000 crores.

items.statement: Announced JV for 25 acres in North Bengaluru with potential GDV of Rs. 3,300 crores.
items.quote: In May, we basically have announced a JV with KVN, Property Holding Limited LLP for approximately 25 acres land parcel located in North Bengaluru with a potential GDV of Rs. 3,300 crores and a planned saleable area of approximately 3.5 million square feet.

items.statement: Launched Purva Panorama in Thane with GDV of Rs. 4,000 crores, starting with Tower C.
items.quote: We successfully launched our much-awaited Project Purva Panorama in Thane, Mumbai, with a total development potentia l of 3 million square feet, with estimated GDV of Rs. 4,000 crores, commencing with Tower C, which covers 0.52 million square feet.

items.statement: Commercial projects Zentech and Aerocity expected to generate surplus of Rs. 1,870 crores.
items.quote: We have two projects, one is Zentech and Aerocity. And they both are in Bangalore. And these two projects are exp ected to generate a surplus of Rs. 1,870 crores, making a significant value creation opportunity for the company.

items.statement: Expects margins to improve with recent acquisitions.
items.quote: I think with the kind of acquisitions that we have done, we should see those margins improve.

items.statement: Sustenance sales achieved with price increases across projects.
items.quote: And Ashish, just to add to that point is that our sustenance sales has come at a price increase, so there has been a decent price increase across all our sustenance projects.

items.statement: Demand sentiment is good and momentum continues.
items.quote: No, I think the demand sentiment is good on the side, on the ground. Whatever the project that we are there is, okay, just if I have to put a reverse corollary to that one that you are asking, whether we are maintaining the same momentum.

items.statement: NGT issue in Mumbai may delay launches; resolution expected by September.
items.quote: So, on our Mumbai portfolio, just since you started with Andheri, Lokhandwala, our approvals, excluding the N GT which is MOEF, everything is going as per the plan. We are in the final stages of securing IROD, but however, this NGT issue is pending in Supreme Court, so it will be difficult for me to give you any timeline for that.

items.statement: Organizational restructuring to regional CEO structure for efficiency.
items.quote: So therefore, the new structure is where we have a CEO for the South region, who manage the entire South business. We have a CEO for the West region, who manages the entire, and both then report into the MD.

items.statement: Focus on residential business in key markets: Mumbai, Pune, Chennai, Hyderabad, Bangalore.
items.quote: In terms of growth aspirations, we continue to focus on the markets where we are present, which is Bombay, Pune, Chennai, Hyderabad and Bangalore, so these are the key markets, where we will continue to expand.

items.statement: Land acquisition strategy focuses on ready projects to market within 6-10 months.
items.quote: So right now, we are looking at ready projects where we are able to give advances and take them to market within six months. I think the minute you are able to do that and get your land assets into production, I think that's the key, that's our business that we are in, as opposed to aggregating smaller pieces of land, incurring holding costs, etc., etc.

items.statement: Aims to grow top line by 15% to 18%.
items.quote: I think the whole plan is that on the top line we grow by 15% to 18% that is what we are aiming to do and let us hope for the best.

items.statement: Expects to continuously grow by 15% to 18% every year.
items.quote: Yes, Mr. Arup, as you see that we are continuously adding new projects, new verticals in our line of business and the whole idea is that to continuously grow by 15% to 18% every year.

items.statement: Expects PSU and government projects to grow by at least 15%.
items.quote: I think we are expecting good numbers, good business from the PSU and government projects while continuing this upward trend, I think we will be growing by at least 15% in this sector also.

items.statement: Feels will continue to maintain margins and hopes they get better.
items.quote: So, we feel that we will continue to maintain these numbers and we only hope that they will only get better in coming quarters.

items.statement: No major impact on India-US trade lane; expects business to grow further.
items.quote: So, Aditya overall there has not been any major impact on our business as far as the India-US trade lane is concerned. In fact, we are happy because globally people are at least, the US buyers are looking at India more seriously now.

items.statement: CUBOX LCL product expected to contribute significantly to revenue.
items.quote: So, we are hopeful that because it has just been three months and market has accepted the product in a very positive way and in coming quarters also this is going to contribute in a big way, in a good way to our whole revenue.

items.statement: Tariff war stabilized, not a threat for India-US business.
items.quote: So, we are seeing that the tariff war is more or less stabilized. It is no more a threat as such, I think we should not we worried about the tariff part on the India-US business is concerned.

items.statement: Aims to be top five logistics company in India.
items.quote: I would say in the next three to four years we want to be in the top five logistics company in India.

items.statement: Snowman Logistics plans capex of Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 150 crores per year for warehousing capacity and vehicles.
items.quote: Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 150 crores per year. Even Gateway is Rs. 30 crores per year. So, say Rs. 60 crores for the next two years. This is basically some warehousing capacity and vehicles.

items.statement: Gateway Distriparks plans capex of around Rs. 30 crores per year, excluding new terminals.
items.quote: So, maybe around Rs. 30 crores, other than the new terminals.

items.statement: Capex will be funded 80% through loans and 20% from internal accruals.
items.quote: Yes, we are still of the same opinion that we go with 80-20 model. 20 will be from our internal accruals, 80 will be funded through loans.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 volumes expected to be much better, in line with Q2-Q4 FY25.
items.quote: So, because Q1 was low, this Q1 will be much better, say more in line with what we have done Q2, Q3, Q4. So, you will see some growth there.

items.statement: Double stacking percentage targeted to increase to 42%-43% going forward.
items.quote: And going forward also as the volumes grow, we are anticipating a good amount of increase. So, we are targeting 42%-43% going forward.

items.statement: 5PL gross margins expected to remain in the range of 6% to 8% depending on product mix.
items.quote: Yes, correct. That is changed , but it will remain in the range of 6 % to 8% depending upon the product mix.

items.statement: About 4% to 5% pricing increase achieved with existing customers on renewals this year.
items.quote: But on average, across most of our existing customers who we do renewals with, then about 4% to 5% pricing increase we have this year. 4%.

items.statement: Volumes expected to remain around the same range with some growth, more from market share gains.
items.quote: Overall also, sentiments are lower, fresh investments are less. So, volume will probably remain around the same range with some growth. More growth we are getting from gaining market share.

items.statement: Warehousing margins impacted by shift to Park 'n' Pay model and Amazon business shutdown.
items.quote: So, some of it is contributed by the “Park ‘n’ Pay” model. This year we have grown 500 x in “Park ‘n’ Pay” model wherein close to 60,000 pallets were outsourced and built. So, wherein the margins are lower, thus the percentage margin is pulled down on the warehousing part.

items.statement: Land acquisition for new ICDs remains challenging; company reevaluating plans due to lower sentiment.
items.quote: So the plan remains the same. But as we mentioned over the last few calls that land acquisition continues to be a big challenge. We have almost finalized a couple of parcels and then due diligence doesn't go through.

items.statement: No plans to merge Snowman into GDL or increase stake immediately.
items.quote: So, no plans of merger right now as the y are different businesses. Regarding stake also, we haven't thought of anything yet. We are not against it, but we don't have any immediate plans to increase our stake either.

items.statement: Jaipur land acquisition under Benami Property Act; company confident of favorable tribunal outcome within 1-2 years.
items.quote: We are hopeful within the next year or two, for whatever reason, this got caught in this legal case. But according to us, it's still fine.

items.statement: Snowman added two new 5PL customers: Unilever and Kopi Kenangan.
items.quote: So, this year we have added two new customers. One is Unilever and the other one is an Indonesian coffee chain by the name Kopi Kenangan.

items.statement: Kolkata facility starting in June, adding 6,000 pallets; Krishnapatnam phase 1 in July.
items.quote: Hi, see the facility in Calcutta is starting in the month of June itself and it will add additionally almost 6,000 pallets.

items.statement: Warehousing business grew 5% excluding Amazon, but Amazon loss of Rs. 10-11 crores offset topline.
items.quote: If we remove Amazon business alone, from the “Park ‘n’ Pay” and the dry business, it's around 5% increase we can see in a warehousing business, which is exactly been compensated by loss of Amazon business in the topline, which is around Rs. 10-11 crores, works out to be.

items.statement: Foreign combined ratio expected to improve to around 110% or 115% by year end.
items.quote: Yes, currently it is at 121 % something, and we still want to improve , if it can be around 110 % or 115% that will be an achievement by the year end.

items.statement: Overall combined ratio expected to improve to around 106% or 107%.
items.quote: Yes, around 106%, 107% figure.

items.statement: Project measured growth of about 10% year-on-year for the next three years.
items.quote: On an overall basis, we project growth in our reinsurance business, which will be measured growth of about 10% year-on-year for the next three years.

items.statement: Health portfolio growth expected in the range of 5% to 10%.
items.quote: So , hopefully if the same trend is continued and if the companies are prepared to accept the same terms, then the growth would be in the range of say 5% to 10%, but the percentage of growth that we have seen this year is not likely to continue going forward.

items.statement: Fire segment market expected to grow by 10% to 20% due to IRDA rates.
items.quote: The pricing, as I said, we are seeing the growth, particularly the companies are following up the IRDA rates, which itself will help the market to grow by 10 % to 20% in the fire segment.

items.statement: Life claims trend not expected to continue; claims expected to settle down.
items.quote: And we believe that if you just talk about coming quarters, obviously, we do not expect this kind of trend will continue. We hope that it will settle down.

items.statement: International market pricing is soft except for loss-affected non-proportional treaties with 10-15% loadings.
items.quote: Pricing, I would say pricing international market what I saw in the 1st January renewal is quite soft, so far direct market is concerned. And both in domestic and foreign, it is quite soft. Except for the accounts where there are some losses, and those treaties particularly, the non-proportional treaties would attract some of the loadings ranging from 10% to 15%.

items.statement: If obligatory business goes away, there could be a temporary setback to top line.
items.quote: Prayesh, in this situation, if obligatory goes away, yes, there could be a hit, a temporary setback to the top line . But on the flip side , it gives us greater control on our portfolio.

items.statement: Foreign motor and marine tail risks continue but are waning; enough reserves created.
items.quote: I would not say it has come to an end. Obviously, such an arrangement has a tail. I can only say that the contract that we cancelled by the end of 2021, the effect of it is waning. The tail continues. It has not come to an end, but it is certainly waning . And more importantly, we have created enough reserves in our books of account as well.

items.statement: CAT reserve corpus planned to build up to Rs. 5,000 crores; no drawdown until then.
items.quote: So this reserve is being created in line with the CAT reserve policy as approved by the Board and we plan to build up this corpus to some thing like an amount of Rs. 5,000 crores. Till that corpus is built, we do not plan to recover or withdraw draw down from this reserve.

items.statement: Rating upgrade in November 2024 led to new international accounts in January renewal.
items.quote: The 4th Quarter growth is mainly resulting from the rating upgrade of G IC wherein we got the rating upgrade in the month of November '24. And that has been passed on to our insurance and reinsurance. And based upon the information , we are able to write some of the new accounts in the January renewal, and that has catered to the growth in international business in the 4th Quarter.

items.statement: International growth from rating upgrade expected to continue as new accounts are offered.
items.quote: Yes. Now that we got our rating back and the international market is aware of it , and no doubt they are coming and offering the new accounts to us , or wherever we lost the accounts we are trying to regain them. So naturally this process will continue going forward.

items.statement: Domestic loss ratio 85.33% and foreign loss ratio 96.5% for full year.
items.quote: The loss ratio for the domestic portfolio annually is at 85.3%. And for foreign business it is 98.9%.

items.statement: Investment income full year Rs. 11,204 crores; interest/dividend Rs. 7,096 crores; profit on sale Rs. 4,108 crores.
items.value: Rs. 11,204 crores, Rs. 7,096 crores, Rs. 4,108 crores
items.quote: The breakup is, for the full year investment income stands at Rs. 11,204 crores. The income excluding profit, that is your interest, dividend stands at Rs. 7,096 crores., which is a 10% increase from the previous year of Rs. 6,430 crores, profit on sale is Rs. 4,108 crores as again Rs. 4,135 crores.

items.statement: Q4 investment income breakup: Rs. 1,500 crores profit on sale, balance interest and dividend.
items.quote: Yes. For the quarter the breakup will be say around Rs. 1,500 crores from profit on sale and the balance will be interest income, so interest and dividend income.

items.statement: Expects 25% growth in Fluoropolymers from current levels.
items.quote: I mean Fluoropolymer, what we are seeing the traction right now, we expect to see almost 25% growth in Fluoropolymers from where we are today.

items.statement: Announced capex of INR1,600 crores for FY26, with INR1,200 crores for GFCL EV and INR400 crores for GFL.
items.quote: We have announced capex of INR1,600 crores for FY '26 with INR1,200 crores earmarked for GFCL EV, largely towards increasing the current capacities with increased customer approvals and audits in pl ace and INR400 crores for GFL, largely earmarked for Fluoropolymers and refrigerant business.

items.statement: Expects R-32 commercial sales to start in second half of FY26.
items.quote: We are also working on multiple options to initiate the commissioning of R-32 plant much ahead of the schedule and expect to commence the commercial sale starting during the second half of this financial year.

items.statement: Expects EV business revenue to trickle in towards second half of FY26 and ramp up in FY27.
items.quote: We expect the revenue from EV business to trickle in towards the second half of this financial year. I would not say sizable because GFL, of course, is a fully grown business. But nevertheless, we expect the ramp-up to continue and pick up in FY '27.

items.statement: Anticipates margin and volume improvements in Specialty Chemicals in FY26.
items.quote: Specialty Chemicals remained stable, and we anticipate margin and volume improvements going forward in FY '26.

items.statement: Expects R-22 price increase as global production quotas reduce.
items.quote: Within our Fluorochemicals business, we saw improvement in R -22 prices during the quarter and further increase is expected as global production quotas reduce.

items.statement: Bulk Chemicals segment faced production loss and price softening, expected to normalize.
items.quote: During the quarter, our Bulk Chemicals segment faced challenges due to an incident at our -- one of our plants in Dahej, CMS -1 plant, leading to approximately 15% production loss and softening of MDC prices have negatively impacted our profitability in this segment.

items.statement: Working capital days increased due to inventory build-up, expected to normalize in 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: Also, working capital days have increased in anticipation of the growth in next few quarters. We have increased production of Fluoropolymers and Vacuum materials to build up the pipeline, and we expect this to normalize in next 1 to 2 quarters.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR1,451 crores as of March 31, 2025.
items.quote: Our net debt as on March 31, 2025 has come down to INR 1,451 crores as compared to INR 1,769 crores as on March 31, 2024, resulting an improvement of net debt to equity from 0.3% to 0.2%.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 28% to INR305 crores with margins improving to 25%.
items.quote: Our EBITDA grew significantly by 28% to INR305 crores with margins improving from 25% -- to 25% from 21% in same time last year, which is quarter 4 FY '24.

items.statement: PAT nearly doubled to INR191 crores in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: Our consolidated PAT nearly doubled, reaching INR191 crores in this quarter.

items.statement: Revenue from operations increased 8% year-on-year to INR1,225 crores.
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that for the quarter, we have reported revenue from operations of INR1,225 crores, reflecting an 8% increase year-on-year.

items.statement: Expects power and fuel savings of INR120-150 crores annually, trickling in partly this financial year.
items.quote: So as we indicated earlier also, the total saving will be in the tune of INR 120 crores to INR150 crores on an annualized basis, but that will trickle in partly this financial year and based on the -- as and when the facilities comes up.

items.statement: R-32 capex indicated at around INR150 crores, excluding HF.
items.quote: Yes, Meet, in fact, in the last quarter call, we had indicated a capex of around INR150 crores, okay? So we are still holding on to that capex , and we'll see how it -- the capacity addition actually takes place with respect to how much we can add in our existing available capacities in the existing plants and how much we'll have to build up the new.

items.statement: Targets 20,000 tons R-32 capacity, holding on to target.
items.quote: But our target, of course, is FY 20,000 that we had indicated earlier, which will possibly be a combination of retrofitting as well as if we are not able to get that much volume, it will be the capacity capex additions. So it will be the combination of the two. However, the target is 20,000. That's -- we are holding on to that target.

items.statement: Expects working capital cycle for EV business to be similar to Fluoropolymers.
items.quote: We expect it to be similar because in this case, also since our target market is -- a big chunk of that is outside India. So we will have to be supplying material to US, for example. There will be material which will be on the high seas. We'll have to maintain certain lev el of stocks. So we should be very similar to our Fluoropolymers, Naushad.

items.statement: Board approved brownfield expansion at Bhavnagar for an SCC global molecule, investing INR 55 crore to double capacity.
items.quote: With the further investment of about INR 55 crore, and with this we are targeting to double the capacities. And it will also means this entire additional capacities can be used to expand our exports to our parent Company. This plant is expected to be completed by Q4 Financial Year 2026-27.

items.statement: Brownfield project at Tarapur for a newly launched global molecule with estimated CAPEX less than Rs. 10 crore, completion by Q4 FY27.
items.quote: The estimated CAPEX for this project is less than Rs. 10 crore. And the timelines are very similar to the first Brownfield project of Bhavnagar. So, the Tarapur Brownfield project is also expected to be completed by Financial Year '26-'27, Q4.

items.statement: Dahej greenfield plant for multiple products, initial investment Rs. 300 crore, manufacturing to start between FY27 and FY30.
items.quote: We plan to invest, as informed earlier, an initial investment of Rs. 300 crore to start with and we are prepared for more investment depending on the number of products we finalize and the time that will be required to put up each and every plant.

items.statement: Endeavor to increase margin compared to FY25, with new high-margin products and demand generation.
items.quote: Our endeavor is to increase the margin compared to what we delivered in FY '24-'25.

items.statement: EBITDA margin may exceed 20% if trend of focusing on high-margin products continues.
items.quote: So, we have already broken that ceiling and from the mindset point of view also, now we understand that since we are not focusing on the top line growth, since we are not focusing on some of the low margin product, naturally the margin profile will go beyond 20% and it may go beyond 20% if the trend continues like this.

items.statement: Expects volume growth in FY26 due to early monsoon, positive sentiments, and increased acreage in key crops.
items.quote: There is definitely going to be a volume growth. I think, I just saw, I didn't read it. MSP prices have been announced just maybe half an hour back. I didn't read it yet. I am sure it has gone up at least 5% to 10% on key crops.

items.statement: Prices have bottomed out and may inch up from current levels.
items.quote: And also we are not really seeing any further price drop because prices are quite stable. Whatever has happened has happened and I think if at all the price can only inch up from this level, that is what we feel.

items.statement: Commercialization of Excalia Max and Lentigo expected to enhance competitive position in key crop segments.
items.quote: The commercialization of Excalia Max and Lentigo, both high potential patented molecules from SCC, is expected to significantly enhance our competitive position in key crop segments.

items.statement: Plan to introduce 3 to 4 products under 9(4) registration in India.
items.quote: Apart from SCC molecules, we are also poised to introduce another 3 to 4 products under 9(4) registration in India.

items.statement: Export markets present selective challenges, particularly in Latin America.
items.quote: While export markets present selective challenges, particularly in Latin America, our agile approach, expanding footprint in Africa and Asia, and robust product pipeline will help balance risks and capitalize on emerging opportunities.

items.statement: In discussions with parent for semiconductor chemicals expansion in India, no decision yet.
items.quote: And we are in discussions with them. And we are jointly evaluating the opportunities in India. No decision has been made at this point of time.

items.statement: Excalia Max technical to be manufactured in India within 12 to 15 months at Tarapur plant.
items.quote: Before that, I think it is also important to mention that the technical or the active ingredient, as we call it, for this newly launched globally blockbuster product will also be made by us in India within next 12 to 15 months.

items.statement: Bhavnagar expansion to meet 40% to 50% of global requirement for the molecule.
items.quote: This facility will enhance our ability to support the global requirement of very important SCC molecules and SCIL will be able to meet 40% to 50% of the global requirement.

items.statement: 100% of domestic demand for the new product expected to be met from India production in next two years.
items.quote: And with this, the 100% of the domestic demand in India is expected to be met from the production from India in next two years or so.

items.statement: Isostearic acid export volumes to increase in first half of FY26, then further scale up in second half.
items.quote: We anticipate a staggered increase in export volumes with the initial pickup expected in the first half of 25-26, followed by further scale up in second half.

items.statement: Isostearic acid to gradually pick up over next 6 months, then further in second half of FY26.
items.quote: Isostearic acid is gradually picking up. It will take further 6 months. In the first half of this financial year, it would pick up compared to the previous 6 months. And again, in the second hal f of this current financial year, it will further pick up

items.statement: Optimum utilization of Isostearic acid expected by next year.
items.quote: By next year, we should reach the optimum utilization.

items.statement: 16 customer approvals received for Isostearic acid; commercial orders have started.
items.quote: Around 16 approvals we have got.

items.statement: New product plant equipment ordered, delivery in 6 months, trials in Jan-Mar.
items.quote: We have ordered the equipment, which will take 6 months to come. because all these are specialty equipments. And so it will take around 6 months for us to receive the equipment and then before end of December, we should have all the equipment and we start trials in January, March period.

items.statement: 40,000 tons of capacity earmarked for new product out of 120,000 tons total.
items.quote: I think in one of our previous con calls or in our presentation, we have already stated that out of our installed capacity of 120,000 metric tons per annum in terms of throughput of raw material, we have already earmarked 1/3rd, that is 40,000 tons of capacity for this new product.

items.statement: Working on energy saving, yield improvement, and new raw material to improve EBITDA margins.
items.quote: On a positive note, I would like to say that we have started working on energy saving, yields improvement and at the same time, we have started working on a new raw material, which can help us mitigate this additional custom duty cost and reduce our raw material cost, which will help us in improving our EBITDA margins.

items.statement: 22% additional custom duty on key raw material since Sep 14, 2024, caused cost escalation; unable to pass on due to Chinese competition.
items.quote: A key challenge since last 2 quarters is the 22% additional custom duty imposed on the key raw material used for manufacturing of our prime product dimer fatty acid, which came into effect on September 14, 2024. As anticipated, this has resulted in sharp cost escalation. Unfortunately, the cost burden could not be passed on to customers due to pricing pressure from Chinese competitors who are not

items.statement: Paint industry demand to revive in October-December quarter due to monsoon slowdown.
items.quote: The way things are going on I don't think we should be bullish for the paint industry because this quarter is going to be the monsoon period. And typically, during monsoon period, paint activity is always on the lower side. So probably we can expect things to revive back in October -December quarter for the paint industry per se.

items.statement: Supplies to paint industry dropped but not significant; sold 5,500 tons in Jan-Mar vs 4,674.
items.quote: We could sell approximately 5,500 tons in the January-March quarter compared to 4,674. So for the quarter per se, it is a high. But compared to the earlier 2 quarters, it is showing a fall.

items.statement: Representation to government for custom duty reversal uncertain; unlikely to receive substantial attention.
items.quote: Being the only player in India, it is really tough. We are trying our best, but I cannot say when it will happen.

items.statement: Cannot predict paint demand for next 2-3 years due to end-consumer dependence.
items.quote: See, ultimately, see, you have to understand one thing that we are supplying to paint sector and paint sector ultimately is supplying to the end consumer. So it will be very difficult to predict what will happen in the next 2-3 years as far as paint demand from paint sector for our product is concerned.

items.statement: No guidance given; may update in Q2 concall.
items.quote: No, not yet. We think maybe in Q2 concall when there is there, we might.

items.statement: Revenue target for next fiscal year is INR 1,000 crores with continued emphasis on maintaining or improving EBITDA margins.
items.quote: Our revenue target for the next fiscal year is INR 1,000 crores with continued emphasis on maintaining or improving EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins to improve from current 16% to between 18% and 20%.
items.quote: We are expecting our EBITDA margins to improve from current 16% to between 18% and 20% as we are committed to increasing profitability.

items.statement: Plans capex of over INR 200 crore over 2 years, with INR 52 crore at existing facility and INR 64 crore at Shalvis Specialities.
items.quote: We have targeted a capex of over INR 200 crore over 2 years with planned capital expenditures of INR 52 crore at our existing facility and INR 64 crore at Shalvis Specialities Limited.

items.statement: Total capital expenditure of about INR 116 crore budgeted for FY26.
items.quote: Our capacity expansion initiatives are progressing well as planned with a total capital expenditure of about INR 116 crore budgeted for FY '26.

items.statement: Projects 15% to 20% revenue growth in next 2 to 3 years.
items.quote: So we are projecting 15% to 20% revenue growth in near next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Sees significant jumps at 20% compounded in next 2 to 3 years from Pretilachlor molecule.
items.quote: We have increased capacity of this product significantly and in the process of further increasing this capacity. So, we see significant jumps at 20% compounded in next 2 to 3 years from this molecule.

items.statement: Feels 10% to 15% demand growth in key molecules Captan, Prosulfocarb, Folpet.
items.quote: And demand, we feel 10% to 15% demand growth in these molecules.

items.statement: Raw material prices are getting stabilized and are more or less stable now.
items.quote: And on the prices, on the raw material side, now raw material prices are getting stabilized and they are more or less stable now. There is no severe difference in the raw materials over the small period this time.

items.statement: Export demand is picking up; oversupply from Chinese manufacturers is slowly reducing.
items.quote: Export side demand is also picking up madam now. There has been -- in the last years, the oversupply was there from Chinese manufacturer, but now slowly it is getting reduced and the demand is increasing.

items.statement: Antidumping duty on Pretilachlor has been recommended but not yet notified; notification pending with Ministry of Finance.
items.quote: The antidumping has not been notified yet. It has been recommended by Ministry of Commerce, but it has not been notified yet.

items.statement: Formulations business growing more than 20% compounded; bulk formulation exports increased to around INR 50 crore.
items.quote: Our Formulations business is growing, say, more than 20% compounded. In this current year, we have also exported bulk formulation, which was very small earlier.

items.statement: Working capital days expected to come down by 10 to 15 days in coming quarters.
items.quote: They will come down, but they will be slightly higher than historical level. They will come down definitely by 10 to 15 days in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Around 55% of revenue should happen in first half.
items.quote: Yes, yes. 55% should happen -- around 55% should happen in first half.

items.statement: Expects higher margin every quarter between 18% to 20%.
items.quote: We are expecting higher margin every quarter between the range of, say, 18% to 20%. In some quarter, it may be on lower band. In some quarter, it may be on higher band.

items.statement: Peak revenue from Sandila unit expected around INR 1,100 crore.
items.quote: Peak revenue, it will be around, I think, INR 1,100 crore we can easily move from Sandila only.

items.statement: Pretilachlor capacity of 8,500 tons expected by August; value more than INR 300 crores.
items.quote: 8,500 tons is the Pretilachlor if you take, sir, now that value here should be more than INR 300 crores.

items.statement: Initial revenue from cell culture to begin in Q4, full-scale ramp-up in FY27 and FY28.
items.quote: We anticipate that initial revenue contributions from the cell culture to begin in Q4 of this year and a full-scale revenue ramp-up in FY '27 and '28.

items.statement: Expects industry revival in second half of FY26.
items.quote: These indicators strengthen our optimism for a broader industry revival in the second half of FY '26.

items.statement: Expects similar CAGR growth in near future as historical 16-18%.
items.quote: Historically, Tarsons has grown at a CAGR in the 16% to 18% category range. So I think we are still short by about 15-odd percent for further growth. So I believe that in the near future, we should see similar levels of CAGR growth for Tarsons, that is our expectation.

items.statement: Expects exports to grow faster than domestic in FY26.

items.statement: Peaton Electrical will have a very good year compared to last year even without new products.

items.quote: So about INR 60 crores plus INR 20 crores, around INR 70 crores, INR 80 crores is the capex, which we can expect on the top line for the next 2 years.

items.statement: Anticipates positive EBITDA for die-casting by end of FY26.
items.quote: So we anticipate that this transition will lead us to positive EBITDA by end of financial year '26.

items.statement: Expects strong growth driven by EMS and solar sectors.
items.quote: In particular, we expect a strong growth to be driven by EMS and solar sectors, both of which are seeing robust demand and align well with our product capabilities and long-term strategy.

items.statement: Automotive sector pressure may persist for next few months.
items.quote: Several OEMs have instigated product line cuts leading to a reduction in order volumes, a trend that may persist for next few months.

items.quote: So we still want to do business with them as long as the contracts are flexible. What we're saying to them is, okay, you want to supply, then here is our proposal. So we agree on the price.

items.statement: Expects double-digit growth in electronics business this year.
items.quote: So I don't see any challenges on that. So it is -- like we still will have double-digit growth this year, but it's not with what we are doing.

items.statement: Targets US revenue of $5-6 million in coming years.
items.quote: Now this year, we have a much similar target, and we feel that for the coming few years, this kind of growth we can expect until we reach something like $5 million to $6 million there.

items.statement: Expects Solar UNO single phase inverter rollout in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: This will be rolled out of R&D from Rishabh. And in Q1 FY '26, we a re expecting this to be rolling out.

items.statement: Expects ND50 power quality analyzer by end of this financial year.
items.quote: We call this product as ND50. This is expected by end of this financial year.

items.quote: Then medium voltage current transformer and potential transformers will be rolled out in next 1year [inaudible 0:28:19], will be coming from electromechanical R&D of Rishabh.

items.statement: Expects 4-5% organic growth in non-auto die-casting business.
items.quote: So non-auto business, which is not having those turbulences and challenges on profitability. That is something which we want to grow, with some organic growth, we can expect 4%, 5%, not more.

items.statement: Expects 100% year-on-year growth in EMS business.
items.quote: So this has given 100% year-on-year growth in the last financial year.

items.statement: Expects 20% top line growth in China operations.
items.quote: Our operations in China has shown a healthy top line growth. We grew by 20% there.

items.statement: Company aims to grow overall top line by more than 35% in FY26.
items.quote: So, in terms of top line at EPACK, we are definitely looking to grow overall by more than 35%.

items.statement: Company aims to maintain EBITDA margins at 7.5% plus in FY26.
items.quote: So, we'd like to maintain our EBITDA margins at 7.5% plus. So that's the kind of EBITDA margin guidance we'd like to give, while maintaining the overall PAT.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin guidance is around 8% plus/minus.
items.quote: Overall, if you look at medium term for next 2 to 3 years, we are looking at an EBITDA margin of around 8% plus/minus.

items.statement: Company plans to invest INR450-500 crores over next 12-18 months for manufacturing expansion.
items.quote: We plan to invest approximately INR 450 crores to INR 500 crores over t he next 12 to 18 months to expand manufacturing capabilities and support our wholly owned subsidiary to cater to increasing market demand for FY '27 and onwards.

items.statement: Company plans to increase plants from 4 to 6 and customers from 55 to 70 in FY26.
items.quote: We have already shared this in our investor deck. So, we are looking to increase plant from 4 to 6 in the current financial year, increase customers from 55 to 70 again in this financial year and also increase product categories and reduce newer product categories as well.

items.statement: Industry expected to grow 15-20% in FY26; EPACK aims to surpass market growth.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 demand impacted by unseasonal rains; some slowdown in lifting finished goods.
items.quote: So Arshia, in terms of Q1, currently, I think it's more of a wait-and-watch situation as the brands are evaluating the overall demand being lifted or the inventory in the pipeline. So, currently, yes, there is some slowdown in terms of lifting the finished goods.

items.statement: Washing machine production to ramp up from end of June, full-fledged from Q3 FY26.
items.quote: So Q2 being the -- of FY '26 being the first month, we will look at establishing and ramping up production and then getting full-fledged from Q3 of FY '26.

items.statement: Air coolers revenue expected to double in FY26.
items.quote: And we are definitely looking coolers to grow twofold in this year.

items.statement: New greenfield JV Epavo to commence production from Q2 FY26 with 3 million AC motor capacity.

items.statement: Price increase with some customers helped increase margin by around 2% year-on-year.
items.quote: One of the main reasons was that there was a price increase with some of the customers, and which helped us to increase the margin on a year-on basis around 2%.

items.statement: Promoter pledge to be withdrawn by end of next quarter.
items.quote: Yes, by end of the next quarter, the pledge would be withdrawn.

items.statement: Confident to deliver high-teen growth in revenue and EBITDA margin for FY26.
items.quote: For this year 25-26, we are now confident to deliver high-teen growth, both in terms of revenue as well in terms of EBITDA margin.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected around Rs. 300-320 crore.
items.quote: So, about Rs. 65 crore for this, so Rs. 65 crore and Rs. 160 crore is about 225 and another Rs. 80 crore to Rs. 100 crore will be on the project so around Rs. 300 crore-Rs. 320 crore that is the normal spend which is spent for the CAPEX this year.

items.quote: So, on an overall basis, I think over the next five years, the CAPEX plan is roughly in the range of around Rs. 1,700 crore to Rs. 1,800 crore depending upon existing and future acquisitions, but Atul will give you the breakups in greater detail.

items.statement: Signed deals for 206 asset-light keys to open in FY26.

items.statement: Target to add 500 keys annually on asset-light model.
items.quote: The overall target on the asset light side of the model remains at 500 keys every year.

items.statement: Aim to improve margins by 100-200 basis points.

items.statement: Flurys EBITDA margin was 12% for FY25.
items.quote: And we have recorded an EBITDA margin of 12% in the Flurys business for this year.

items.statement: Flurys post-rental margin expected 8-9%.
items.quote: Post rental the margin should be around 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Hospitality sector entering long-term super cycle over next decade.
items.quote: As I have highlighted in the previous call, we believe that the hospitality sector is entering a long -term super cycle and would unfold over the next decade.

items.quote: So, we are going to be changing the mix of this business from higher kiosks to cafes as we go forward. And we will make all efforts to see that it becomes further profitable.

And our successful war against Pakistan in May and we are proud that we could defeat them. But that has had some sort of an impact on the growth.

items.statement: Board approved maiden dividend of 50%.
items.quote: I am delighted that our Board has approved a maiden dividend of 50%, a reflection of our performance and our commitment to sharing our success with our partners.

items.statement: Juhu property expected to add Rs. 25-30 crore EBITDA in full year.

items.statement: Kolkata service apartments to generate Rs. 100 crore annual cash flow over three years.

items.statement: Revenue growth of 40% to 50% over current year's revenue expected.
items.quote: So we want to be on very conservative side. That's why he has said that we can expect a revenue growth of 40% to 50% over current year's revenue.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 14% to 16% on total revenue.

items.quote: The revenue will start picking up from the Q2 onwards. In fact, Q1 would also be better as compared to the past years , but the actual pick up will start from quarter two onwards.

items.quote: Yes, no, no, I mean, actually, two of the opportunities are, you know, very much on the finalizing stage and it could get finalized in the next one or two months itself and both are comparatively quite significant value.

items.statement: INR 70 crores revenue slipped to current financial year due to external factors.

items.statement: Average execution cycle around 1.5 to 2 years.
items.quote: Average execution cycle could be around 1.5 years to 2 years.

items.statement: Hopeful to clock 25% CAGR growth over next three years.
items.quote: With the opportunities in the existing MICE setup and with the new developments in place, we are hopeful to clock a growth of 25% CAGR over next three years.

items.statement: Hopeful to achieve FY24 profitability ratios this year.
items.quote: But this year, we are hopeful that we will be able to achieve 2024 profitability ratios.

items.statement: Not much significant business expected from B2C verticals in current year.
items.quote: Overall, we understand that there will not be much significant business coming from the B2C verticals because everybody would need some time to penetrate and get the business onto the table.

items.statement: MICE will remain bread and butter, not losing focus.
items.quote: You know, our bread and butter would remain at MICE, we are not losing the focus.

items.statement: Trademark dispute for B2C portal is in court, no comment.

items.statement: Acquisition of Travexel Events and Travel to complete in about 30 days.
items.quote: The agreements have been signed and everything is in place, but the entire thing will be executed in about 30 days from now.

items.statement: Became aggressive in quoting, lowering markups and profit margins.

items.statement: BFSI sector downturn in Q3 impacted business.
items.quote: And since the BFSI segment was down in the third quarter, we became a little aggressive in the fourth quarter and picked up businesses at an aggressive this thing.

items.statement: Received INR25-27 crores of INR47 crores receivables.
items.quote: No, the good news is that out of the INR47 crores, INR25 crores to 27 crores we 've already received as we speak and the balance we would be getting soon.

items.statement: Kumbh event revenue about 20 lakhs with 18-19% profitability.
items.quote: Now, the Kumbh event, the revenue was not too much, I think about 20 lakhs or something with the profitability of surprisingly 18% to 19%.

items.statement: Considering quarterly updates, seeking advice.
items.quote: You know, we had thought about it. We are still contemplating. We would seek advice and, you know, this is the foundation of the company in terms of the IPO listing.

items.statement: Expected annual growth rate of 35% to 40% with EBITDA margins of 22% to 24%.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we aim to sustain our growth trajectory with an expected annual growth rate of 35% to 40%, while maintaining healthy EBITDA margins in the range of 22% to 24%.

items.statement: Order inflow of INR 1,000 to 1,250 crores expected from bids submitted.
items.quote: Even if we go by a conservative number of somewhere around 20% to 25%, even at that level, we can expect that an order inflow of INR 1,000 to INR 1,250 crores that should accrue to the Company from the bids that we have already submitted.

items.statement: Target to build order book of INR 2,500 to 3,000 crores in current financial year.
items.quote: So, every quarter, if we can have that number of somewhere around maybe 750-1000 odd crores of order book available to us and if we can build up that order book of around INR 2,500 crores to 3,000 crores in this current financial year.

items.quote: Right now, from our GCP, from the IPO funds, we have proposed an investment of INR 50 crores in EIE Renewables. Through our discussions, we have kept that overall investment from Enviro Infra to EI E Renewables at a maximum of INR 75 crores.

items.statement: Renewable sector EBITDA margin expected around 18-20%, not below.
items.quote: are visualizing some of the projects, we have definitely submitted some bids, wher ein we have in those stands, 22%, 24% of EBITDA margins in the renewable sector, to my understanding, might not be possible, but yes, to an extent of around 18 -20% is the margin what we are looking for. We will not go down beyond that.

items.statement: Right mix of EPC and HAM projects at 75:25 ratio going forward.
items.quote: HAM project drives better margins in comparison to EPC projects, but we cannot be, go very heavy on HAM. So, we will always be having a right mix between EPC and HAM .
